title: FFT / NTT & polynomial multiplication (stretch)
relevance: Medium — almost never a literal OA template (Striver omits this entirely); shows up only in hard screens as “count ways / match strings under large n” once you already know generating functions.
company_notes: Almost never asked to code FFT in a timed OA; if it appears, it’s disguised as equal-sum/product halves with n small enough for DP—still recognize the generating-function shape. Harder OAs sometimes ask minimum Hamming/wildcard matches with n~10^5 (FFT convolution of indicators; hashing+BS may substitute). Unlimited knapsack / exactly k items under large sums → poly power; interviewers want GF insight more than butterflies. XOR/bitmask combine-by-index in researchy screens → FWHT.

phases.goal: Candidate spots a convolution / polynomial-multiply bottleneck instead of nested O(n^2) loops.

must_hit.point: Bottleneck is convolution c_k = sum_{i+j=k} a_i b_j (multiply polys, raise a GF to a power, count alignments/Hamming mismatches, XOR/OR of masks).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They name convolution or poly multiply and map the sum-of-products-over-i+j=k shape to FFT/NTT.

must_hit.point: Signals: n ~ 10^5–10^6 and the formula looks like a sum of products over i+j=k; also pairwise products, digit-sum halves, subset color vectors, wildcard/multi-alphabet string matching.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They cite large n plus pairwise/i+j=k structure, or string-FFT / GF-counting flavors.

must_hit.point: Later toolkit siblings: XOR convolution via FWHT; online / divide-and-conquer FFT when DP transitions are convolutions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They mention FWHT for XOR or CDQ/online FFT for f[i] depending on earlier f via convolution.

probes: What pattern in the formula or constraints makes you reach for FFT/NTT instead of nested loops?

hints.1: Look for sums of products indexed by i+j=k.
hints.2: That sum is convolution—equivalent to multiplying two polynomials.
hints.3: Replace O(n^2) nested loops with FFT/NTT in O(n log n) when n is ~10^5–10^6 and the formula is that convolution.

phases.goal: Candidate chooses FFT vs NTT vs FWHT/online-FFT and sketches the right high-level plan.

must_hit.point: FFT = DFT over complex numbers (watch precision; round to nearest int); NTT = same butterfly over prime p = c·2^k+1 with a primitive 2^k-th root (no floats; default mod 998244353).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They contrast complex FFT + rounding vs modular NTT on an NTT-friendly prime like 998244353.

must_hit.point: Prefer NTT whenever the statement is mod an NTT-friendly prime; for arbitrary/non-NTT mod use split coeffs + CRT (3 NTT mods) or long double FFT with care.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They say NTT first under friendly mod, and CRT/long-double FFT when the modulus is not NTT-friendly.

must_hit.point: Poly power via binary expo of polys (P^k) for exactly k summands; string FFT reverses the pattern and uses 0/1 (or ±1) indicator arrays; XOR uses FWHT on length 2^k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They outline P^k, reverse-pattern indicator convolutions, or FWHT for XOR convolution.

probes: When would you use NTT instead of complex FFT, and what changes for XOR convolution or string Hamming?

hints.1: Check whether the modulus is NTT-friendly.
hints.2: Same butterflies: over C for FFT, over p = c·2^k+1 for NTT; XOR needs FWHT.
hints.3: Default NTT mod 998244353 with g=3; string matching reverses the pattern into indicator polys; XOR is c_k = sum_{i⊕j=k} a_i b_j via FWHT.

phases.goal: Candidate can describe a correct multiply / power / string-FFT pipeline, including padding and inverse scaling.

must_hit.point: FFT multiply: pad to length 2^{ceil(log_2(n+m-1))}, forward DFT both, pointwise multiply, inverse DFT, divide by n, round.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They list pad → DFT → pointwise → IDFT → divide by n → round.

must_hit.point: NTT multiply: same butterflies over mod p = c·2^k+1 (stock 998244353, g=3); precompute roots; no floating error.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They mention iterative butterflies, bit-reverse, precomputed roots under 998244353 with g=3.

must_hit.point: String FFT: reverse pattern; 0/1 indicators per alphabet symbol; wildcard/Hamming via sum (P_j - T_{i+j})^2 expanded into 2–3 convolutions; online/D&C FFT recurses mid, convolves left→right, then solves right.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They describe reverse + indicators + a few convolutions, or mid-split online convolution for DP.

probes: Walk through multiplying two polynomials with NTT, including length and the inverse step.

hints.1: You need a power-of-two length that fits the full product.
hints.2: Pad to 2^{ceil(log_2(n+m-1))}, transform both, multiply pointwise, invert.
hints.3: After inverse DFT divide by n and round for FFT; for NTT use roots mod 998244353 (g=3) with no floats.

phases.goal: Candidate states the asymptotic win of transforms over naive convolution.

must_hit.point: Naive nested loops for convolution are O(n^2); FFT/NTT multiply is O(n log n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explicitly contrast O(n^2) with O(n log n).

must_hit.point: FWHT does XOR convolution in O(n log n) on length 2^k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They give O(n log n) for FWHT on a power-of-two length.

probes: What is the complexity of FFT/NTT polynomial multiplication versus the naive double loop?

hints.1: Compare nested loops to a transform-based multiply.
hints.2: Naive convolution is quadratic in the degree/length.
hints.3: FFT/NTT (and FWHT for XOR) run in O(n log n).

phases.goal: Candidate anticipates precision, modulus, and reachability mistakes that break FFT/NTT solutions.

must_hit.point: Complex FFT needs careful precision and rounding to nearest int; prefer NTT when the mod is NTT-friendly to avoid floating error.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They warn about float error/rounding and switch to NTT under 998244353-style mods.

must_hit.point: For arbitrary/non-NTT modulus, precision can die with long double FFT—use split coeffs + CRT (3 NTT mods) or treat carefully as in cp-algo arbitrary modulus.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They name CRT with 3 NTT mods or acknowledge when float FFT precision fails.

must_hit.point: For poly power reachability-only problems, clamp nonzero coeffs to 1; ship a battle-tested iterative butterfly + bit-reverse template (or ACL atcoder::convolution / convolution_ll when allowed).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They mention clamping support coeffs and relying on a known template/ACL convolution.

probes: What goes wrong if you use complex FFT under a modular statement, or forget clamping in a reachability poly-power?

hints.1: Think about floating error versus modular butterflies.
hints.2: NTT-friendly primes avoid floats; arbitrary mods need CRT or careful FFT.
hints.3: Round/precision failures on C; use NTT/CRT instead; for reachability-only P^k clamp nonzero coeffs to 1.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: FFT is DFT over C—fast but needs precision care and rounding to nearest int. NTT uses the same butterflies over p = c·2^k+1 with a primitive 2^k-th root (stock 998244353, g=3)—no floats. Prefer NTT whenever the statement is mod an NTT-friendly prime.

tradeoffs.topic: Own NTT template vs ACL convolution
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Implement your own iterative butterflies + bit-reverse once as a milestone, then allow ACL atcoder::convolution / convolution_ll in contests that permit the library.

tradeoffs.topic: Interview GF insight vs coding butterflies
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For knapsack/exactly-k / lucky-ticket shapes, interviewers usually want the generating-function insight (poly power / halves) more than hand-rolled FFT butterflies; OAs almost never ask to code FFT literally.

tradeoffs.topic: String FFT vs hashing + binary search
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Interview-friendly answer for large Hamming/wildcard matching is FFT convolution of indicators; some screens still accept hashing + BS as a substitute.

gotchas.trap: Treating FFT like exact arithmetic and skipping rounding / precision checks.
gotchas.correction: FFT is over C—watch precision and round to nearest int; prefer NTT when the mod is NTT-friendly.

gotchas.trap: Using a single complex FFT under an arbitrary modulus and trusting the coeffs.
gotchas.correction: For non-NTT mods, split coeffs + CRT (3 NTT mods) or use long double FFT carefully; know when precision dies.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting to pad before DFT so the product wraps or truncates.
gotchas.correction: Pad to length 2^{ceil(log_2(n+m-1))} before forward transforms.

gotchas.trap: Leaving full multiplicities when only reachability of totals matters (e.g. Thief-style P^k).
gotchas.correction: Optionally power in frequency domain for support only, and clamp nonzero coeffs to 1.

gotchas.trap: Using cyclic NTT for XOR-of-indices combination.
gotchas.correction: XOR convolution needs FWHT (Hadamard) on length 2^k, not ordinary cyclic NTT—Binary Table / Nim Counting family.
